text:
emily: Quick follow-up after today's all-hands runtime roadmap section. Need to pin a few things so PM/Docs/Infra can move: 1) Which sprint are sparse-attention kernels vs quantization landing? 2) What is the default KV eviction policy customers see on Hosted? 3) Suggested default auto-batching knobs for Hosted vs Dedicated (batch_ms, max_batch_tokens, prewarm). Please keep answers short so I can paste them into the notes. @sam @raj @lisa
sam: TL;DR: sparse-attn in current sprint but behind a gating PR; quantization work starts next sprint (planning this week). Hosted default eviction = LRU, tenants can opt into TTL-based eviction. We're experimenting with adaptive batch_ms as a follow-up.
raj: For defaults: Hosted: batch_ms=12 and max_batch_tokens=4096 is a good balance (keeps p95 ~120-140ms for chat baseline). Dedicated: if you enable prewarm, batch_ms=25 and max_batch_tokens=8192 yields best unit-cost for steady traffic. Note long contexts (>6k) are where sparse-attn really helps, so we'll prioritize quant on 2k-4k models first.
lisa: I'll prepare a tiny CSV with measured p50/p95/p99 and cost deltas by batch_ms bucket (5/12/20/25) and share with PMs. ETA: Wednesday COB.
kevin: Ops note: p99 spikes still correlate with cold-starts and oversized requests. I've added a trace attribute `cold_start=true` for kernels so SRE dashboards can filter. Also linking rollback/playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/kernel-release (see section 3.2 rollback).
dina: Can we get a concise config snippet for docs to show "safe defaults" + tenant override example? PM wants a copy-ready block.
sam: Sure, dropping example (feel free to adapt):
```
runtime_defaults:
  batching:
    batch_ms: 12
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    adaptive: true  # runtime can lower batch_ms under high tail latency
  kv_cache:
    policy: LRU
    ttl_seconds: 0  # tenant can set >0 to enable TTL-first eviction
  prewarm_window_ms: 1000
```
maria: From PM side: please include a small column for "expected cost delta" in that CSV (rough ballpark is fine). Sales needs numbers to discuss tradeoffs.
lisa: Will add cost column (approx %) and assumptions row (chat baseline: 8 tokens/sec user, median seq length 256).
raj: Ops sizing follow-up: for Dedicated pools we should publish recommended prewarm sizes per model family. I'll draft guidance after Lisa's numbers.
dina: Filing tracking ticket: DOC-8219 to publish docs + PM table.

emily: Great, can someone post a 2-line summary for the all-hands notes with owners + ETA? I just need one sentence per item (kernel timing, kv default, batching defaults, owners).
sam: I'll post the 2-line summary here by EOD today.
